reviewNote: DRAFT, unreviewed by any Hebrew teacher and not yet tried by a learner. Every Hebrew string is copied from an existing data file named in `source`; nothing here is new Hebrew. The minutes are a design budget, not a measurement.
goal: Five short steps, one screen each: one letter, a second letter, one vowel sign, one syllable, one real word. The on-ramp is lesson r01 taken one piece at a time; finishing it completes r01.

steps.title: Your first letter: Shin
steps.action: Tap Hear it. Then tap Trace it and draw it once with your finger.

steps.title: Your second letter: Bet
steps.action: Tap Hear it. Then trace it once.

steps.title: Your first vowel mark: the small T
steps.action: Look under the letter. The small T-shaped mark is a vowel mark. Tap Hear it.
steps.win: Win 3 of 5: your first vowel mark.
steps.source: data/pronunciation/niqqud.json (kamatz.shape = base letter bet with the sign); the sound line comes from the same record in your tradition

check.prompt: Which one has the vowel mark under it?

steps.title: Your first syllable
steps.action: Letter first, then the vowel mark under it. Shin plus the small T. Say it aloud, then tap Hear it.
steps.win: Win 4 of 5: you practised a syllable.

check.prompt: Which one is Shin with its vowel mark?

steps.title: Your first word
steps.action: Shin with its vowel mark, then Bet with no dot inside. Say it aloud, then tap Hear it.
steps.win: Win 5 of 5: you practised a real Hebrew word.
steps.source: data/curriculum/lessons.json r01.words[0]; respelling from data/vocab/words.json h842147e5 (translit shav) via the transliteration engine for your tradition

done.title: Five wins. You read your first Hebrew word.
done.body: שָׁב (shav) means "returned". You just read a real Hebrew word, with its vowel marks. The next lesson adds one more letter and the dot inside Bet, so you can read שַׁבָּת (Shabbat).
done.tomorrow: Come back tomorrow for your next letter.
done.preview: Optional preview: read שָׁלוֹם today (about 10 minutes). Lesson 3 teaches these letters properly; this is a head start, not a shortcut.
